chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight kinds of source ingests well, ingests with loss, or needs extra work first, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** ingestion-path-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight kinds of source ingests well, ingests with loss, or needs extra work first, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Document Ingestion, File Access, Open File Format (defined in Chapter 4) (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 4). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each source the learner commits one of three bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A PDF ingests as well as the document it came from. (2) A picture of text is text. (3) A video can be read directly. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging how well a source ingests is an Evaluate-level action that applies what the learner knows about editable formats to the work of an agent. Eight sources across three bins teach the learner to ask where the structure lives. **Content:** The three bins: Ingests well (text and structure come through), Ingests with loss (text comes through, and structure or order may be damaged), and Needs extra work first (the source must be converted before an agent can read it). The eight sources: | # | Source shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A Markdown file | Ingests well | Its structure is in the text. | | 2 | An HTML page | Ingests well | Headings, links, and alt text are in the markup. | | 3 | A word processing document | Ingests well | Text and headings extract cleanly, with only small formatting loss. | | 4 | A PDF made from a word processor | Ingests with loss | The text comes through, and the reading order, headings, and tables may be scrambled. | | 5 | A scanned PDF that is a picture of each page | Needs extra work first | It must be run through text recognition before there is any text. | | 6 | A slide deck | Ingests with loss | The text in boxes comes through, and the order and any images are uncertain. | | 7 | A video lecture | Needs extra work first | It must be turned into a transcript first. | | 8 | An image of a chart | Needs extra work first | The values must be described or extracted first. | **Provenance:** The sources are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The judgments follow the chapter section "Document Ingestion". **Rules:** Each source has exactly one correct bin. Three sources are Ingests well, two are Ingests with loss, and three are Needs extra work first. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one source and the three bins. 2. The learner places the source in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After source 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 sources in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You know which sources an agent can read." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed source. **Starting State:** The first source and the three bins. The question shown is "How well will this source ingest?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says Markdown and HTML ingest cleanly, a PDF made from a document often ingests with damage, and a scan or a video needs conversion first.
